findings.message: T011 is not executable as written: it leaves the `architecture-rules.json` schema change open between an opt-in verifier block and an explicit layer-role field, so the implementer has to invent the schema shape before coding.

T012 is not executable as written: it leaves the `review-scope.json` sync strategy open between deriving patterns from `architecture-rules.json` and moving the mapping into `overlay`, so the source of truth is undefined.

task-coverage.json has no mapping for any goal element. The impl-plan severity policy requires GO-NN elements to be covered alongside IN/OS/CN/AC, but GO-01 through GO-05 are absent entirely, so the plan can pass lower-level coverage without preserving top-level traceability for the export goal, bootstrap separation, placeholder workspace, manifest/overlay boundary, and D5 genericity prerequisites.

T010 is mapped to OS-10 and CN-09, but the task text only says to run export and then `cargo make ci` in the output tree. It does not carry the OS-10/CN-09 constraint that the smoke gate must not hard-fail user-owned areas such as provider settings, permission policy, signal strictness, or user domain code, making this coverage implausible for a load-bearing exclusion.

T012 requires `.harness/config/review-scope.json` to derive per-layer review patterns from `architecture-rules.json` "at load time", but the task names only config/docs files and no loader file or symbol where that runtime derivation is implemented. An executor would have to discover and invent the code boundary, so the task is not executable as written.

task-coverage.json has no formal mapping for GO-01 through GO-05; it only maps in_scope, out_of_scope, constraints, and acceptance_criteria. The rendered goal traceability summary is not a task-coverage mapping, so the GO elements are uncovered under the impl-plan severity policy.

T004 restates the export behavior contract in prose: walking the workspace, classifying paths, copying Include, skipping Exclude, applying Overlay, and fail-closed error cases. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, this should be target + operation + anchor cite only so it cannot drift from IN-01/IN-03/AC-01/AC-03/CN-03.

T007 restates upstream boundary and bootstrap rules in prose, including which paths are include/exclude/overlay and how bootstrap reads the pinned tag and invokes cargo install. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, keep this as target + operation + anchor cite only.

T008 restates the upstream template-workspace contract: the exact 6-crate layout, absence of vendor patch/[patch.crates-io]/lancedb, and architecture-customizer premise. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, these behavioral details should remain behind IN-04/AC-04/CN-05 anchors.

T009 restates upstream genericity requirements, including no sotp-specific vendor build steps and no sotp-specific ADR/research references in overlay track docs. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, this should be reduced to target + operation + anchor cite.

T010 restates the smoke-gate behavior contract step by step, including output-tree CI behavior, non-zero propagation, and exclusion of user-owned hard-fail areas. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, those details should be anchored to AC-05/OS-10/CN-09 rather than restated here.

T011 restates the verifier-genericity contract: verify flags, target path resolution from architecture-rules, and preservation of equivalent sotp checks. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, keep the task to the files/symbols to modify plus IN-08/AC-08/CN-07 anchors.

T012 restates the harness-config alignment contract, including deriving review patterns, aligning catalogue-lint layers, resolving the apps/cli-composition vs apps/cli conflict, and arch-rules-derived catalogue references. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, this should be target + operation + anchor cite only.

T013 restates the provenance-removal behavior contract across harness docs, including which references to remove and the exception for sotp-context in ADRs/commit messages. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, those requirements should be represented by IN-10/AC-10/AC-12 anchors, not prose.

T014 restates the Python-leftover removal contract by listing the exact .tool-versions and .gitignore tokens to remove and verify. Per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md, this should be target + operation + IN-11/AC-11/AC-12 anchors only.

CN-05 is mapped to T008, but T008 only says to author placeholder workspace files and an overlay-file-existence test; it does not require excluding sotp source, vendor patches, `[patch.crates-io] conch-parser`, or lancedb deps from the overlay Cargo workspace files it owns. That makes the CN-05 coverage load-bearing but implausible for the task that authors those files.

CN-10 is mapped to T007/T011/T012, but those tasks do not carry any active-track-only/no-retroactive-migration/no-compatibility-layer step. Since T011 and T012 change verifier and harness rule loading, CN-10 is load-bearing there; the current mapping can pass structurally while leaving the constraint unenforced in the executable plan.

T002 attributes `TemplateBoundaryManifestReadError` in `task-contract.json`, but the task description tells the implementer to add `TemplateBoundaryManifestReadError (NotFound / Parse / Invalid / Io)`. The attributed usecase catalogue entry splits that invalid case into `InvalidPattern` and `InvalidManifest`; following this plan would implement the wrong enum surface and miss the catalogue contract.

T003 attributes `TemplateBoundaryManifestCodecError`, but the task description specifies `Domain { source } + From<TemplateBoundaryManifestError>`. The attributed infrastructure catalogue entry requires separate `Pattern` and `Manifest` variants, including pattern-error conversion; following the plan as written would omit part of the declared entry and implement a non-catalogue `Domain` variant.

task-coverage.json still has no formal mapping for GO-01 through GO-05; it only maps in_scope, out_of_scope, constraints, and acceptance_criteria. The impl-plan summary's goal traceability line is not a task-coverage mapping, so the GO elements remain uncovered under the impl-plan severity policy.

T007 restates upstream behavior in prose: "bootstrap-host-only protoc / sotp MSRV requirements" and "no archive migration or default compatibility layer" repeat CN-05/CN-10 instead of using target + operation + anchor cite only, contrary to knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

T008 restates the CN-05/AC-06 workspace-exclusion contract in prose ("exclude sotp source / vendor patches / conch-parser patch / lancedb deps") instead of keeping the task to target + operation + anchor cite per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

T011 restates CN-10 behavior ("scoped to active tracks only, with no archive migration or default compatibility layer") rather than relying on the CN-10 anchor, violating knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

T012 restates CN-10 behavior ("scoped to active tracks only" and "without archive migration or default compatibility layer") rather than relying on the CN-10 anchor, violating knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

Section S5 repeats upstream behavior in its section description (bootstrap-host-only prerequisites, active-track-only schema application, Cargo dependency exclusions) instead of limiting the section to target + operation + anchor cites per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

Section S7 repeats CN-10/CN-08 behavior in its section description (active-track-only dispatch/loading and no archive/default compatibility behavior) instead of limiting the section to target + operation + anchor cites per knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md.

AC-03 omits T007 even though T007 authors overlay/Makefile.toml and the bootstrap task, while AC-03 explicitly covers static overlay files including Makefile/bootstrap tasks. That leaves a load-bearing AC-03 slice mapped only to tasks that do not own that file.

AC-06 maps only T007, but T008 is the task that edits the overlay Cargo workspace and explicitly excludes sotp source, vendor patches, conch-parser patch, and lancedb deps. The AC-06 workspace-exclusion requirement is therefore not covered by the task that implements it.

IN-12 omits T003 even though T003 owns the schema-versioned manifest DTO and decode_manifest validation path. The schema/read-stability part of IN-12 is load-bearing in the codec task but is not mapped there.

CN-04 omits T009 even though T009 authors overlay/architecture-rules.json, which CN-04 explicitly includes in the out-of-the-box CI consistency contract. The architecture-rules portion is not tracked on its owning task.

`task-coverage.json` claims several out-of-scope alternatives are covered by T007 (`OS-01` through `OS-04`, `OS-08`, `OS-11`), but T007 only authors the boundary manifest/bootstrap artifacts and related tests. There is no executable step or anchor in T007 for avoiding physical repo split, GitHub release binaries, lancedb feature-gating, or historical archive migration, so these mappings are load-bearing but implausible coverage rather than real plan coverage.

T001's task text restates upstream behavior instead of staying at target + operation + anchor cite. The validation details (`non-empty`, forward-slash-only, no leading `/` or `..` segment) and manifest invariant details duplicate the IN-02/IN-12/AC-02/CN-02 contract in prose, which violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`. Keep the file/symbol additions and anchors, but remove the behavior restatement from the impl plan.

T007 restates upstream behavior in prose: "the export walker only substitutes overlay content for EXISTING workspace paths, so net-new overlay-only files cannot be emitted". Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, keep this task to target + operation + anchor cite only; the same prose is mirrored in `plan.md`.

T008 adds explanatory prose for the root `Cargo.toml` edit (`so overlay placeholder crates do not join the sotp cargo workspace`). That restates the intended effect instead of staying in the required target + operation + anchor format; trim it and regenerate `plan.md` from the updated impl-plan. See `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

P1, bootstrap: `install-sotp` shells out to `jq` to read `.harness/config/sotp-version.json`, but the bootstrap flow never checks for or installs jq. On a clean host without jq, `cargo make bootstrap` will fail midway with a shell error instead of a declared prerequisite. See [overlay/Makefile.toml](/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/overlay/Makefile.toml:101).

P1, testing: the new public `GreetUser::execute` API only has a success-path test. The error branch where `SalutationProvider::salutation` returns `Err(GreetError::Unavailable)` is unverified, so the `?` propagation contract is not covered. See [overlay/libs/usecase/src/lib.rs](/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/overlay/libs/usecase/src/lib.rs:51) and the existing happy-path-only test at [overlay/libs/usecase/src/lib.rs](/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/overlay/libs/usecase/src/lib.rs:76).

P1, testing: the new public `GreetDriver::run` API is only exercised on the happy path. Add a failure-path test that injects an erroring `SalutationProvider` so the `success: false` rendering branch is covered. See [overlay/apps/cli-driver/src/lib.rs](/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/overlay/apps/cli-driver/src/lib.rs:30) and the current success-only test at [overlay/apps/cli-driver/src/lib.rs](/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/overlay/apps/cli-driver/src/lib.rs:57).

Fresh exports intentionally omit Cargo.lock, but the template CI tasks still invoke Cargo with --locked. During `cargo make bootstrap`, Step 5 runs `ci-local`; the first locked Cargo gate such as `clippy-local` will fail in a newly exported tree before consumers have generated a lockfile. Either generate Cargo.lock before CI or drop `--locked` from the exported template gates.

`ci-local` still includes `verify-tech-stack-local`, while the exported `track/tech-stack.md` is intentionally TODO-seeded. In a fresh export there are no track dirs and no `.track-template-dev` marker, so `sotp verify tech-stack` treats those consumer-owned TODO values as fatal and `cargo make bootstrap`/`cargo make ci` fails before project setup. This violates the stated deviation that the export gate must not hard-fail on consumer-owned configuration values.

D2 says the template bootstrap will not build sotp source, but the selected command is `cargo install --git`, which compiles the git source on the bootstrap host. That conflicts with the same ADR's grounding that protoc/MSRV/vendored dependencies constrain building sotp, not running a prebuilt binary, and later claims consumers are separated from those build constraints. Downstream spec/impl-plan cannot derive whether bootstrap must provision sotp build prerequisites or switch to a prebuilt/feature-gated distribution path.

P1: `TemplatePathPattern::try_new` accepts syntactically distinct but semantically identical paths like `libs/domain` and `./libs/domain`, while `TemplateBoundaryManifest::try_new` only checks duplicates by raw string equality. That lets the same workspace path appear twice with different classifications, bypassing the fail-closed duplicate guard and making `classify()` depend on the caller's spelling instead of the actual path. See [libs/domain/src/template_export/mod.rs:33](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/libs/domain/src/template_export/mod.rs#L33) and [libs/domain/src/template_export/mod.rs:141](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-004/libs/domain/src/template_export/mod.rs#L141).

`TemplatePathPattern::try_new` preserves a trailing `/` in the normalized value, so semantically identical workspace paths like `vendor` and `vendor/` become distinct `TemplatePathPattern`s. That lets `TemplateBoundaryManifest::try_new` accept conflicting rows for the same path and makes `classify()` depend on spelling rather than path identity.

`TemplatePathPattern::try_new` returns `TemplateBoundaryManifestError`, but this constructor can only fail while validating a single pattern; the shared enum also exposes `DuplicatePattern` and `EmptyManifest`, which this method cannot structurally produce. The method docs do not list the producible subset or justify the wider error surface, so callers must handle impossible variants.

`TemplateBoundaryManifest::try_new` also returns the full `TemplateBoundaryManifestError`, but it receives already validated `TemplatePathEntry` values and its docs only describe duplicate/empty checks; `InvalidPattern` cannot be produced at this layer. Split the pattern/manifest errors or explicitly declare the reachable subset for each constructor.

`TemplateExportReport` cites `AC-05`, but that acceptance criterion is about running `cargo make ci` on the exported workspace and adding a smoke gate, not the successful-export report DTO. This is an off-topic `spec_refs` anchor for this entry.

`FsTemplateExportAdapter` also cites `AC-05`, but the adapter contract is copying/excluding/overlaying files; `AC-05` is the separate smoke-gate/CI-green requirement. Keeping that anchor here makes the adapter appear responsible for CI verification.

Domain catalogue docs restate upstream behavior instead of just naming the target and citing anchors: `TemplatePathPattern` restates path-shape validation, `TemplatePathClassification` restates Include/Exclude/Overlay effects, and `TemplateBoundaryManifest` restates classification and uniqueness behavior. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` forbids this in `<layer>-types.json` docs because the behavior contract belongs in spec/ADR anchors.

Usecase catalogue docs restate upstream behavior across `TemplateExportCommand`, `TemplateExportReport`, `TemplateExportError`, `TemplateExportService`, `TemplateBoundaryManifestPort`, and `TemplateExportPort` by describing pass-through paths, counts, fail-closed policy, manifest reading, tree filtering, overlay application, and copy/skip/replace behavior. These should be reduced to target/operation plus `IN-*`/`AC-*`/`CN-*` cites per the no-upstream-restatement convention.

Infrastructure catalogue docs restate upstream behavior in `FsTemplateBoundaryManifestAdapter`, `FsTemplateExportAdapter`, `TemplateBoundaryManifestDto`, `TemplatePathEntryDto`, `TemplatePathClassificationDto`, `TemplateBoundaryManifestCodecError`, and `decode_manifest` by describing JSON reads, workspace walking, overlay-copy behavior, raw-string validation, mirror literal sets, schema mismatch/JSON/domain failure modes, and parse-to-domain behavior. Those behavior details should live behind the cited spec anchors, not be duplicated in the catalogue docs.

CLI-driver docs restate downstream behavior in `TemplateExportInput`, `TemplateInput`, `TemplateDriver`, and `TemplateDriver::handle`, including boundary import rationale, future variant behavior, service invocation, report/error rendering, stdout/stderr, and exit-code behavior. Per no-upstream-restatement, the catalogue should cite the relevant anchors rather than carrying those behavioral contracts itself.

CLI catalogue docs restate command behavior in `TemplateCommand`, `TemplateExportArgs`, `CliCommand`, `cli::commands::template::execute`, and `cli::commands::template::dispatch`, including future subcommand shape, flag mapping, Template dispatch, composition-root outcome mapping, and exit-code mapping. These duplicate upstream CLI/export behavior and should be anchor-only contract descriptions.

`TemplateCompositionRoot` and its methods restate wiring behavior by naming concrete adapters, interactor construction, driver injection, and error mapping. That wiring behavior is upstream contract content for `IN-01`/`AC-01`; the catalogue docs should not duplicate it in prose.

`TemplateBoundaryManifest` now documents that entries are unique and prefix-free in prose. The types severity policy flags upstream restatement in `<layer>-types.json` docs/intent because downstream catalogues must cite the spec anchors rather than restating behavior; this creates a second source of truth for the manifest invariants. Keep this entry anchor-only and let IN-02/IN-12/AC-02/CN-02 carry the behavior text.

`template-export-smoke-local` is not portable to the exported template: it hardcodes `--overlay-dir overlay`, but `overlay/` is excluded by the boundary manifest (`.harness/config/template-boundary.json`), so the shipped task will fail in a fresh consumer checkout.

The new smoke-task description embeds a source-only path, `libs/infrastructure/src/template_export/codec.rs::test_decode_real_repository_manifest_is_fail_closed_clean`. That file is not present in the exported skeleton, so the distributed Makefile now contains a dead reference to internal test code.

The rewritten workflow now says the dedicated `git sync` command composes the branch switch and ff-only pull, but `git sync` only pulls the current branch; the switch+sync behavior belongs to `cargo make track-switch-base` / `bin/sotp track switch-base`. This makes the done workflow SSoT describe the wrong command boundary, so adapters following it can misroute users toward `bin/sotp git sync` when they need the fail-closed switch-base operation.

`diagnose.md` is still a `.claude/commands/track/*.md` adapter, but its opening contract points only at `.harness/capabilities/rollback-diagnoser.md` and never declares an existing `.harness/workflows/<path>.md` SSoT. The harness-policy adapter-SSoT check requires track command adapters to explicitly name a real workflow SSoT up front and avoid carrying workflow logic locally, so this command remains outside the workflow/adaptor split while embedding trigger, routing, dispatch, and recovery semantics in the adapter itself.

`decode_manifest` deserializes the full `TemplateBoundaryManifestDto` before checking `schema_version`. Because that DTO has `deny_unknown_fields`, a future manifest such as `schema_version: 2` plus a newly added field is rejected as `Json` before the `SchemaVersion` guard runs, despite the codec contract documenting `SchemaVersion` for unsupported versions. This breaks the established versioned-codec pattern used by `agent_profiles.rs` and `dry_check/config.rs`: parse a minimal schema-version envelope first, reject unsupported versions, then parse the strict DTO for the supported schema.

`FsTemplateBoundaryManifestAdapter::read()` dereferences `manifest_path` with `std::fs::read_to_string()` and never rejects a symlinked leaf. This boundary loader is the manifest SSoT entrypoint, and the repo's other security-sensitive loaders reject symlinks before reading; without that check, a symlink can swap in an unexpected manifest and steer export with attacker-controlled classifications.

`copy_tree()` uses `symlink_metadata()` to classify a symlink as a non-directory, then calls `std::fs::copy(source, destination)`, which follows the symlink target. As a result, an included or overlayed subtree can copy bytes from outside the workspace or overlay tree into the exported template instead of rejecting the symlink at the I/O boundary.

`reject_manifest_symlink()` only lstat's the final path component. If `manifest_path` is reached through a symlinked parent directory, `read_to_string()` still follows that chain and loads a manifest from outside the intended tree. The repo's symlink-hardening pattern rejects the whole ancestor chain, not just the leaf.

`export()` starts walking `command.workspace_root` and later resolves `command.overlay_dir` without any root-level symlink check. A symlinked workspace or overlay root can redirect the export outside the intended tree because `read_dir()`/`copy()` follow that root.

`copy_tree` creates the destination directory before enumerating the source. If `command.output_dir` is inside a manifest-included or overlay source directory, the destination becomes a child of the source during the copy, so the recursive walk sees its own output and keeps copying `out/.../out/...` until an I/O failure or disk exhaustion. Add a guard that rejects destinations under the source subtree, or reject output directories under workspace/overlay roots before export starts.

`architecture-rules.json` layer paths are now treated as trusted scan roots without any boundary check. `verify_targets()` builds `<layer.path>/src` directly from config and `check_arch_layers_purity()` then scans it, so a malicious or malformed `path` like `../..` or an absolute path can make the purity verifiers read outside `trusted_root`. The new review-scope drift guard in `review_v2/scope_config_loader.rs` also derives its expected pattern from the same unvalidated `layer.path`, so it can be satisfied by the same escape. This should follow the existing trusted-root pattern used for briefing files: resolve, canonicalize, and reject anything that does not stay under root before scanning.

`validate_layer_groups` treats `architecture-rules.json` as absent whenever `exists()` is false, so a dangling symlink at that path is silently classified as "missing" and the new drift guard is skipped instead of failing closed. That gives a PR author a way to neutralize the layer-group lockstep check by swapping the file for a broken symlink; use the same symlink-aware rejection pattern used elsewhere in the infra loaders before deciding the file is absent.

The config-driven purity scan walks each `<layer>/src` tree with `read_dir`/`read_to_string` but never rejects symlinked directories or files at the boundary. Because `layer.path` now comes from `architecture-rules.json`, a symlinked source tree can make the verifier traverse outside the trusted root; the same pattern exists in `domain_strings.rs` as well.

P1: `validate_layer_groups` only enforces the one-way check from `architecture-rules.json` to `review-scope.json`. If a layer is renamed or deleted in arch-rules, any stale review-scope group with the old layer name is still accepted because there is no reverse check for surplus layer groups. That leaves the drift guard non-fail-closed and can keep routing files into an obsolete scope.
